newsitem.title: UK: S&P says raises Centerbank's ratings.
newsitem.headline: S&P says raises Centerbank's ratings.

text.p: Standard and Poor's said on Friday it had raised Centerbank's subordinated debt rating to A from BB plus.
It also said it raised the bank's long-term counterparty credit rating to A plus from BBB minus.
This debt has been assumed by First Union Bank of Connecticut, S&P said in a statement.
S&P also said the ratings had been removed from CreditWatch, where they were placed on June 17, 1996.
The amount of subordinated debt outstanding is $25 million.
The long-term ratings outlook is stable, S&P said.
The ratings action follows the completion of the acquisition of Centerbank by First Union Bank of Connecticut, a unit of the $133 billion, Charlotte, N.C.-based First Union Corp.
S&P said Centerbank's creditors benefited from the financial and managerial resources associated with the significantly more diversified First Union.
The acquisition not only enhanced First Union's market presence in Connecticut, but also provided cost savings opportunities through the elimination of redundant operations, S&P said.

First Union's outlook was a function of the geographic and product diversity of its core businesses, which should lead to smoother earnings and stable asset quality over the long term, the statement said.
